headline: Whale Monitoring Zones and Activity Reservations
reservation: Entry fees are required for specific land-based interpretation sites and shore-access points managed by Parks Canada or Sépaq. Marine excursions and whale-watching tours are operated by private partners and require separate, advanced bookings during the summer peak. Always verify current zoning restrictions for private boating on the official marine park website.

days.title: Fjord Cliffs and Marine Life

stops.name: Pointe-de-l'Islet
stops.detail: Walk the wooden boardwalks to observe where the Saguenay and St. Lawrence waters meet, often revealing minke whales from shore.

stops.name: CIMM (Marine Mammal Interpretation Centre)
stops.detail: Explore specialized exhibits on cetacean biology and the history of marine research in the estuary.

days.driving: Local walking and short transfers; allow 15 minutes
days.note: Marine air is significantly cooler than inland temperatures; check local maritime forecasts.

days.title: Shore-Based Whale Watching

stops.name: Cap-de-Bon-Désir Interpretation and Observation Centre
stops.detail: Sit on the natural granite rocks to watch for large whales passing close to the shoreline due to the deep underwater canyon.

stops.name: Marine Environment Discovery Centre
stops.detail: Participate in land-based diving activities or view live underwater broadcasts from the St. Lawrence floor.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; Route 138 is the primary artery
days.note: Shore access at Bon-Désir requires walking over uneven rock surfaces.

days.title: Fjord Exploration and Ferries

stops.name: Tadoussac-Baie-Sainte-Catherine Ferry
stops.detail: Take this free transit across the mouth of the Saguenay Fjord, providing a water-level view of the dramatic cliffs.

stops.name: Baie-Éternité (Parc national du Fjord-du-Saguenay)
stops.detail: View the towering Notre-Dame-du-Saguenay statue and the steepest walls of the glacial fjord.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours including ferry wait times; conditions vary
days.note: Ferry queues can be long during summer weekends; allow extra time for transit.

intel.title: Site-Specific Lots
intel.text: Designated parking is available at Cap-de-Bon-Désir and CIMM, but lots are smaller in the historic Tadoussac village. Use peripheral lots if the village core is congested during festival weeks.

intel.title: Rugged Terrain Reception
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in towns but can be intermittent along Route 138 between Escoumins and Sacré-Coeur. Navigation should be downloaded for offline use.

intel.title: Coastal Service Hubs
intel.text: Full services are available in Tadoussac and Les Escoumins. Fueling opportunities become sparser when traveling north toward the Côte-Nord interior.

intel.title: Tidal Cycles
intel.text: Whale activity and ferry boarding can be influenced by tidal movements. Check local tide tables to optimize shore-based observation times.

intel.title: Water Access Regulation
intel.text: Strict speed and distance limits apply to all watercraft to protect marine mammals. Consult the official 'Echo' map for seasonal protection zone boundaries.

plan.arrival: Fly into Saguenay-Bagotville, rent a vehicle, and drive Route 172 or 138 toward the coast, stopping in Chicoutimi for major supplies.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the main highway; RVs should check ferry weight limits and steep grades near the fjord.
plan.goldenHour: Pointe-Noire Interpretation and Observation Centre for views of the fjord at dusk, contingent on cloud cover.
